breakfast.name: Zhingyalov Hats (Herb Flatbread)
ingredients: 500g mixed herbs (parsley, cilantro, dill, sorrel, spinach, green onions)
instructions: Make dough, rest 20 min
Chop herbs finely, mix together
Roll dough thin, fill with herbs, fold and seal
Cook on dry griddle until spotted brown
Brush with butter
breakfast.description: Thin flatbread stuffed with a dozen wild herbs.

breakfast.name: Lahmajun (Armenian Pizza)
instructions: Roll dough into thin circles
Mix lamb with vegetables, paste, spices
Spread thin layer on each circle
Bake at 230°C for 8-10 min
Roll up with lemon juice
breakfast.description: Paper-thin flatbread with spiced lamb topping.

breakfast.name: Lahmajun (Armenian Meat Flatbread)
ingredients: Dough: 500g flour, yeast, water, salt, olive oil
Topping: 400g finely ground lamb, 2 onions (minced), 2 tomatoes (grated), 1 green pepper (minced), parsley, tomato paste, paprika, cumin, Aleppo pepper, lemon juice, salt
instructions: Make thin, soft dough, divide into balls, rest
Mix all topping ingredients — the meat mixture should be almost paste-like
Roll dough balls into very thin circles
Spread thin layer of meat mixture all the way to the edges
Bake on a pizza stone at maximum oven heat (250°C+) for 5-7 min
The base should be crispy, the topping just cooked
Squeeze lemon juice over, add fresh herbs
Roll up and eat by hand
breakfast.description: Armenian meat flatbread — paper-thin crust with a spiced raw meat topping that bakes in minutes. Often called 'Armenian pizza' but far older.

imageCredit.author: No machine-readable author provided. Rainer Zenz assumed (based on copyright claims).

breakfast.name: Jajukh (Yogurt Soup, Cold)
instructions: Whisk yogurt until smooth
Thin with cold water to soup consistency
Add diced cucumber, garlic, dill, mint, salt
Chill thoroughly
Serve cold — especially on hot summer days
breakfast.description: Cold yogurt soup with cucumber and herbs — an Armenian summer staple.

lunch.name: Khorovats (Armenian Barbecue)
instructions: Marinate meat with onions, wine, oil, herbs overnight
Thread onto flat skewers
Grill over charcoal
Grill whole tomatoes and peppers alongside
Serve on lavash with fresh herbs

lunch.name: Dolma (Stuffed Grape Leaves)
instructions: Blanch grape leaves
Mix meat, rice, onions, herbs, spices
Fill leaves, roll tightly
Pack in pot seam-down, add water to cover
Simmer 60 min
Serve with yogurt
lunch.description: Grape leaves stuffed with spiced meat and rice.

lunch.name: Khorovats (Armenian BBQ)
ingredients: Marinade: 2 onions (grated), salt, pepper, sometimes red wine
instructions: Marinate meat in grated onion, salt, pepper for at least 2 hours — some families marinate overnight
Thread onto wide flat metal skewers (not round bamboo — the flat shape prevents spinning)
Grill over charcoal — the mangal (BBQ) is the center of every Armenian gathering
Turn periodically, 20-25 min total — the exterior should char slightly
Grill whole tomatoes and peppers alongside
Slide meat off skewers onto lavash bread
Serve with fresh herb platter (basil, tarragon, cilantro) and sumac onions
lunch.description: Armenia's national BBQ — pork or lamb on flat skewers over charcoal. Every family gathers around the mangal; the person grilling earns the title khorovats-maker.

lunch.name: Ghapama (Stuffed Pumpkin)
ingredients: Dried fruits: apricots, raisins, prunes, dates
instructions: Cut top off pumpkin, scoop out seeds
Mix cooked rice with dried fruits, nuts, honey, cinnamon, butter
Fill pumpkin with rice mixture
Replace pumpkin lid
Bake at 175°C for 75-90 min until pumpkin flesh is very tender
Bring whole pumpkin to the table — guests scoop filling and soft pumpkin flesh together
lunch.description: Festive stuffed pumpkin — the centerpiece of Armenian New Year and wedding tables. There's even a folk song about it: 'Hey jan, Ghapama!'

dinner.name: Ghapama (Stuffed Pumpkin)
instructions: Cut top off pumpkin, scoop seeds
Mix rice with fruits, nuts, honey, butter, spices
Fill pumpkin, replace top
Bake at 180°C for 90 min
Cut into wedges
dinner.description: Festive whole pumpkin stuffed with honeyed rice and dried fruits.

dinner.name: Harissa (Wheat and Chicken Porridge)
instructions: Cook wheat berries 2 hours until very soft
Boil chicken until falling off bone, shred
Add chicken to wheat, stir vigorously
Cook 1 more hour until porridge-like
Top with melted butter and cumin
dinner.description: Slow-cooked porridge traditionally served at Easter.

dinner.name: Tolma (Stuffed Grape Leaves)
ingredients: Filling: 500g ground beef and lamb mix, 1 cup rice, 1 onion (diced), tomato paste, parsley, dill, basil, salt, pepper
Plain yogurt with garlic for serving
instructions: Blanch fresh grape leaves briefly, or rinse jarred ones
Mix raw meat with rice, onion, herbs, tomato paste, salt, pepper
Place spoonful on each leaf, fold sides in, roll tightly
Pack tightly in pot seam-side down
Place plate on top to weigh down
Add water to just cover, simmer 40-45 min
Serve with garlic yogurt
dinner.description: Armenian stuffed grape leaves — the filling includes a trio of fresh herbs. An essential dish for any holiday table.

dinner.name: Harissa (Wheat and Chicken Porridge)
instructions: Simmer wheat berries in large pot with water 2 hours
Meanwhile, boil chicken until very tender, shred meat, discard bones
Add shredded chicken to wheat, continue simmering
Stir frequently — the wheat breaks down into a thick porridge
Cook 1-2 more hours until completely smooth and thick
Stir in butter
Serve in bowls with a well of melted butter and dusting of cinnamon
dinner.description: Ancient Armenian porridge of slow-cooked wheat and chicken — stirred for hours until silky smooth. Made for Easter and religious celebrations.

snacks.name: Gata (Sweet Bread)
ingredients: Filling: 1 cup flour, 1 cup sugar, 100g butter
instructions: Mix dough ingredients
Make filling by crumbling flour, sugar, butter
Roll dough, spread filling, roll up
Shape into round, score top, brush with egg
Bake at 180°C 35 min
snacks.description: Flaky sweet pastry with buttery sugar filling.

snacks.name: Su Börek (Layered Cheese Pastry)
instructions: Boil pasta sheets briefly, lay on damp towels
Mix cheeses with eggs and parsley
Layer: buttered pan, pasta, cheese mixture, pasta, cheese, pasta — repeat
Top layer should be pasta, brushed generously with butter and milk
Bake at 180°C for 30-35 min until golden
Let rest 10 min before cutting into squares
snacks.description: Layers of boiled pasta and cheese filling — brought to Armenia from the Ottoman tradition. The boiled pasta layer makes it uniquely soft and custard-like.

snacks.name: Lahmajun (Armenian Flatbread Pizza)
ingredients: Dough: 3 cups flour, yeast, water, salt, olive oil
Topping: 300g minced lamb, 2 tomatoes (finely diced), 1 onion (finely diced), parsley, red pepper paste, cumin, Aleppo pepper, lemon juice
Fresh lemon wedges, fresh herbs for serving
instructions: Make thin, pliable dough — let rise 30 min
Divide into balls, roll paper-thin — almost translucent
Spread a thin layer of the raw lamb-tomato-spice mixture over entire surface
Bake at highest oven temperature (250°C+) for 6-8 min — the bread crisps, the lamb cooks
The bread should be thin and slightly charred at edges but still pliable enough to roll
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the hot lahmajun
Roll up like a wrap or fold in half
Eat immediately — the crispy-pliable contrast fades quickly
Armenians and Turks both claim this — but the Armenian version is thinner and more lemony
snacks.description: Paper-thin flatbread covered in spiced raw lamb and flash-baked until the meat is cooked and the bread is crispy yet pliable. Squeeze lemon and roll it up. The viral appeal is the speed (6 minutes in a scorching oven) and the satisfying roll-up-and-bite technique. A beloved Armenian street food with ancient roots.

desserts.name: Pakhlava (Armenian Baklava)
ingredients: Syrup: 2 cups sugar, 1 cup water, 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp lemon juice
instructions: Layer phyllo with butter and nut mixture
Cut into diamonds before baking
Bake at 170°C 40 min
Make syrup, pour warm over hot baklava
Soak several hours
desserts.description: Armenian baklava with walnuts, cardamom, and honey.

desserts.name: Gata (Armenian Sweet Bread)
ingredients: Dough: flour, butter, yogurt, yeast, sugar, egg
Khoriz filling: flour, butter, sugar (mixed to crumbly texture)
instructions: Make enriched dough, let rise
Make khoriz: mix flour with softened butter and sugar until crumbly
Roll dough, spread with khoriz, fold and roll again
Shape into rounds or braids
Brush with egg wash, sprinkle sesame seeds
Bake at 180°C for 25-30 min until golden
desserts.description: Armenian sweet bread with a crumbly butter-sugar filling called khoriz. Bakeries shape them in elaborate patterns.

desserts.name: Sujukh (Walnut Churchkhela)
instructions: Thread walnuts onto strings using a needle
Cook grape juice with flour, sugar, and spices until thick and glossy
Dip walnut strings into the thickened grape mixture
Hang to dry 1-2 hours
Dip again — repeat 3-4 times until coating is thick
Hang in cool dry place for 1-2 weeks to firm up
Slice into rounds to serve
desserts.description: Walnut strings coated in thickened grape must — the Armenian candy, cured for weeks and sliced into chewy rounds.

drinks.name: Tan (Yogurt Drink)
instructions: Whisk yogurt smooth
Add water gradually
Season with salt
Serve over ice with mint

drinks.name: Tuti Oghi (Mulberry Vodka)
instructions: Crush mulberries
Ferment 2-3 weeks
Strain and distill
Age 6+ months

drinks.name: Tan (Yogurt Drink)
instructions: Whisk yogurt until smooth
Add cold water gradually, whisk until frothy
Season with salt
Serve cold — the perfect accompaniment to khorovats
drinks.description: Armenian salty yogurt drink — the universal BBQ companion. Called 'tan' and drunk by the pitcher.

drinks.name: Armenian Coffee
instructions: Add coffee, sugar, and cold water to jezve (long-handled pot)
Stir to dissolve
Place on low heat — do not stir once it starts heating
Watch carefully — when foam begins to rise, remove from heat immediately
Let foam settle slightly, return to heat — repeat 2-3 times
Pour gently into demitasse cups, foam first
Let grounds settle 1-2 min before sipping
drinks.description: Armenians call it Armenian coffee (not Turkish). The ritual of reading fortunes from the grounds is a beloved tradition.
